Searching Dryad

Source: vignettes/searching.Rmd
searching.Rmd

dryad_search() wraps GET /search. The package targets Dryad’s production deployment by default; the snippets below assume that. To run the same calls against the sandbox while exploring, prefix the session with dryad_use_sandbox().

library(dryaddata)

Query syntax

The q argument accepts the same shorthand the API does:

  • Multi-term queries are AND-ed: q = "soil carbon" returns datasets matching both terms.
  • Prefix a term with - to negate: q = "carbon -ocean".
  • Append * for prefix matching: q = "soil*".
dryad_search(q = "soil carbon", per_page = 3)

Filtering

The named arguments map straight onto the underlying parameters:

dryad_search(
  q                = "carbon",
  subject          = "soil science",
  orcid            = "0000-0001-7146-8135",
  funder           = "https://ror.org/021nxhr62",
  published_since  = "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  published_before = "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z",
  per_page         = 5
)

dryad_datasets() exposes a similar set of filters but without free text (publication_issn, publication_name, manuscript_number, curation_status).

Pagination

By default you get one page (per_page defaults to 20, max 100). For larger result sets either step manually:

page2 <- dryad_search(q = "soil", page = 2, per_page = 50)

or pull everything with all_pages = TRUE. The result combines the underlying pages into a single records / data block; metadata$pages tells you how many requests were made.

all_soil <- dryad_search(q = "soil", per_page = 100, all_pages = TRUE)
nrow(all_soil$data)
all_soil$metadata$pages

Use max_pages as a circuit breaker for unfamiliar queries:

dryad_search(q = "soil", per_page = 100, all_pages = TRUE, max_pages = 5)

Working with nested fields

Because data keeps complex fields as list-columns, vectorized access is a single vapply() or lapply() away. For example, pulling the primary author from each hit:

hits <- dryad_search(q = "soil", per_page = 5)
vapply(hits$data$authors, function(a) {
  if (length(a)) paste(a[[1]]$firstName, a[[1]]$lastName) else NA_character_
}, character(1))

When you need a fully-flattened representation, the raw records list is trivial to hand to tidyr::unnest_wider() or purrr::map_dfr().
